items.note: Title suggests a study of creativity growth from hybrid AI-human ideation in college programs; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, APA landing page all failed), so design, comparison arm, and N are unknown; included in Shi 2026 meta-analysis per search notes.

Participants use LLM assistance to generate, select, and refine patent-based product ideas under manipulated levels of AI hallucination (one AI configuration versus another); originality, diversity, elaboration, and feasibility are outcomes; N and assignment not in abstract.

Quasi-experiment (per title) comparing traditional, chatbot-assisted, and fully integrated AIGC instruction in a design course; abstract not reachable (publisher elides it), search notes report 100 visual communication design students and pre/post design product performance plus self-efficacy.

Compares traditional versus ChatGPT-assisted inquiry-based learning with 462 Taiwanese high-school students (ANCOVA, PLS-SEM); creativity is one outcome but its measure (test or self-report) and the assignment method are not stated, and the task is not a creative task as such.

Controlled collective word-guessing task comparing human-only, AI-only, and hybrid human-AI groups on performance and diversity of guesses; humans in hybrid groups see AI agents' guesses; assignment and N not in abstract (search notes give 50, 46, 28 humans by arm); task is only partly creative.

Randomized experiment with 435 participants in 122 teams assigned to human-only, single-AI, or multiple-AI teams, plus individual-AI pairs; search notes say blind judges rated quality, novelty, and usefulness; same study as the SSRN version 10.2139/ssrn.4844976.

Randomized experiment with 112 college students comparing AI-first, AI-follow, AI-parallel, and human-only two-stage story writing; narrative creativity rated by 10 trained raters and an AI model; sequential AI collaboration lowered creativity.

Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment with 32 design students comparing a text-and-image AI workflow with human-only brainstorming; three expert raters scored ideation outputs (innovation favored human-only); below 50 participants, and search notes say order was balanced, not randomized.

Title indicates a comparison of AIGC and traditional idea generation methods on creativity in product design ideation; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect all failed), so design and N are unknown; distinct from Lin (2026) PLOS One.

CHI system paper: within-subjects study comparing the Inkspire sketch-driven text-to-image tool with ControlNet (one AI configuration versus another); reports more inspiration and exploration of design ideas, likely self-reported or process measures; N not in abstract; same work as arXiv 2501.18588.
